searchDocs.title: legacyMaps​
searchDocs.content: </> Lanes.legacyMaps( settings: any, partition: string, count: number, lane: number, previous: number? ) → {string} The maps from previous that could hold tickets whose lane, at count, is lane. Only LaneScaler resizes, and it only ever doubles or halves from one, so both counts here are always powers of two. That is what makes this exact rather than approximate. A ticket hashes to h % count: Growing (count > previous): a ticket in old map o satisfies h % previous == o, so its new lane is one of o, o + previous, o + 2*previous, … Reading old map lane % previous therefore covers it. Shrinking (count < previous): h % count == (h % previous) % count, so every old map o with o % count == lane contributes. Either way the result holds at most previous / count entries — one when growing, two on a single halving.

Returns a spread of 0 when no candidate carries ratings, which makes the tie-break on queue time the whole ordering — the right policy for an unrated queue.

searchDocs.title: conflictNext​
searchDocs.content: </> InMemoryStore.conflictNext( self: InMemoryStore, operation: string, count: number?, mutator: ((any) → any)?-- Receives the current value, returns the competing writer's value. Omit to re-run against unchanged state. ) → () Makes the next count updates lose a compare-and-set race: the transform runs once against the value it read, that result is thrown away, mutator installs a competing write, and the transform runs again against the new value — which is what MemoryStore's UpdateAsync does under contention. This is the only way to catch a transform that forgets to reset its own bookkeeping on re-entry, which every conditional write in Muster depends on.

searchDocs.title: Runtime
searchDocs.content: On this page Runtime This item is only intended to be used by the module's authors. Private Show Private The only module in Muster that touches a Roblox global. Everything else receives what it needs through configuration, which is what lets the whole engine run headlessly under Lune against fakes. Each global is read through an any-typed local so the same source typechecks under Roblox (where game exists) and runs under Lune (where it resolves to nil).

searchDocs.title: Metadata​
searchDocs.content: </> type Metadata = {[string]: any} Arbitrary consumer data carried on a ticket. Must survive a JSON round trip through MemoryStore: strings, numbers, booleans, and tables of those. No functions, no Instances, no cycles.

searchDocs.title: Member​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Member { userId: number serverId: string-- JobId of the server that enqueued them. The broadcast address. rating: number?-- Present if and only if the queue is rated. provisional: boolean?-- True when rating.default was substituted for a missing rating. metadata: Metadata? } One player inside a ticket or a finalized match. serverId is per-member rather than per-ticket because a party can span several servers, and each member's own server is the one that needs to hear about the match.

searchDocs.title: Ticket​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Ticket { id: string queue: string partition: string partyId: string? leaderUserId: number members: {Member} size: number rating: number?-- Party-aggregated rating, absent on unrated queues. metadata: Metadata? queuedAt: number expiresAt: number state: "Queued" | "Claimed" | "Matched" | "Cancelled" matchId: string? lane: number-- Index within the partition. laneCount: number-- The lane count in force when it was written; lanes scale at runtime. } A queue entry. One ticket covers one solo player or one whole party — parties are never split across matches.

searchDocs.title: MatchEnvelope​
searchDocs.content: </> interface MatchEnvelope { v: number-- Schema version. matchId: string queue: string partition: string createdAt: number size: number-- Total players across all members. members: {Member} ticketIds: {string} partyIds: {string} data: T-- Whatever your finalize hook returned. } A finalized match, delivered to every server holding one of its members. Generic over the finalizer's return type, so match.data.accessCode is typed and autocompletes. Deduplicate on matchId, never on the set of players — see the finalize contract on Matchmaker.

searchDocs.title: MatchContext​
searchDocs.content: </> interface MatchContext { matchId: string queue: string partition: string members: {Member} ticketIds: {string} partyIds: {string} size: number averageRating: number?-- Mean member rating, absent on unrated queues. createdAt: number deadline: number-- Monotonic time the hook must return by. } What a finalize hook receives. Everything about the match except the decoration the hook itself is about to produce.

searchDocs.title: AbortReason​
searchDocs.content: </> type AbortReason = "FinalizerError" | "FinalizerTimeout" | "FinalizerTooLarge" | "LeaseLost" | "StoreUnavailable" | "TicketStolen" Why a match that had already claimed its tickets failed to commit. FinalizerError — the hook threw. FinalizerTimeout — the hook did not return within finalizeTimeout. FinalizerTooLarge — the hook's return value failed validation or exceeded maxMatchDataBytes. LeaseLost — another server took over this lane while the hook was yielding. StoreUnavailable — MemoryStore rejected the final commit. TicketStolen — a ticket was claimed by another match between selection and commit.

searchDocs.title: AbortContext​
searchDocs.content: </> interface AbortContext { matchId: string queue: string partition: string members: {Member} reason: AbortReason message: string?-- The hook's error text, when reason is FinalizerError. data: any?-- The hook's return value, if it produced one before the abort. } Passed to onAbort. When data is present the hook ran to completion and its side effects survived a match that never formed — that is what this callback is for.

searchDocs.title: Finalizer​
searchDocs.content: </> type Finalizer = (context: MatchContext) → T Runs exactly once per matchId, on whichever server formed the match, after its tickets are claimed and before it commits. Yielding is expected — this is where TeleportService:ReserveServerAsync goes.

searchDocs.title: ErrorCode​

searchDocs.content: </> type Result = { ok: true, value: T } | { ok: false, error: ServiceError } Returned by every method that touches the network. Programming mistakes throw instead — see the error-handling section of the README.

searchDocs.title: Store​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Store {} The storage contract. Muster.stores.MemoryStore implements it against Roblox MemoryStore; Muster.stores.InMemory implements it in a table for tests. Every method returns (success, value) and never throws. update must be a compare-and-set: the transform may be invoked more than once, and returning nil from it must abort the write.

searchDocs.title: Subscription​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Subscription { disconnect: (self: any) → () }

searchDocs.title: Messaging​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Messaging {} The notification contract. Delivery is assumed best-effort and unordered — Muster never depends on a message arriving.

searchDocs.title: Candidate​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Candidate { ticketId: string partyId: string? size: number rating: number? ratings: {number} queuedAt: number } The denormalized view of a ticket that the matcher sees. Deliberately small: it is what gets written into the lane index, and it is read far more often than the ticket itself.

searchDocs.title: MatcherPolicy​
searchDocs.content: </> interface MatcherPolicy { minSize: number targetSize: number maxSize: number fallbackAfter: number-- Seconds before a below-target group is accepted. compatible: ( anchor: Candidate, candidate: Candidate, waitSeconds: number ) → boolean score: ( candidates: {Candidate}, indexes: {number} ) → ( number, number ) } Everything the grouping algorithm knows. Supply your own to replace the rating window with role composition, region affinity, or anything else. score returns (primary, secondary), both minimized, compared in order. The built-in policies use rating spread then total queue time.

searchDocs.title: RatingConfig​
searchDocs.content: </> interface RatingConfig { window: number?-- Starting rating tolerance. Default 200. relax: number?-- Extra tolerance per second waited. Default 40. maxWindow: number?-- Ceiling on the widened window. Default infinite. unbounded: number?-- Seconds after which any rating matches. Default 60. default: number?-- Substituted when a caller omits a rating. Default nil, which makes omission an error. aggregate: (({number}) → number)?-- Party rating from member ratings. Default is a max-biased mean. } Presence of this table is what makes a queue rated. Omit it entirely for an unrated queue, where tickets carry no rating and matching is oldest-first.

searchDocs.title: SizeConfig​
searchDocs.content: </> interface SizeConfig { min: number target: number? max: number? } Match sizing. Muster.new{ size = 6 } is shorthand for all three being 6. A group at target commits immediately; a smaller one waits fallbackAfter seconds before it will settle for anything down to min.

searchDocs.title: EnqueueOptions​
searchDocs.content: </> interface EnqueueOptions { rating: number?-- Required on a rated queue unless rating.default is set. Throws on an unrated queue. metadata: Metadata? partition: string?-- Overrides partitionKey for this ticket. serverId: string?-- Overrides the broadcast address. You almost never want this. }
